Data-quality findings and how they were handled

    03

    Feature selection: five-method consensus + k-curve

    For each target, the learnable variables were ranked by five independent methods (Spearman, mutual information, PLS-VIP, RF permutation importance, Lasso stability over 200 bootstraps). Features were then added one by one and the smallest k within 2% of the best group-CV error (GP and Ridge) was kept.

    04

    How the models performed

    Every model faced three tests: group CV by batch (runs of one batch never sit in both train and test), an edge test (the 20% of batches farthest from the centre of feature space — simulated extrapolation) and a tail test (the top 20% of the target — exactly where we look for the optimum).

    Composite = 0.5 · NRMSEcv + 0.25 · NRMSEedge + 0.25 · NRMSEtail NRMSE = RMSE / SD(y) → 1.0 = no better than predicting the mean

    Composite for every model × four targets

    Lower = better; colour saturates at 2; magenta frame = final model, ● = overall winner

    Three tests, side by side

    Values above 3 are clipped at the edge (▶); hover for the true value
    Group CVEdge (extrapolation)Tail (top 20%)Composite

    Full table —

    Metrac = meta-models

    “Metrac” was implemented as two meta-models: RSM (quadratic response surface with Ridge) and Stacking (non-negative linear blend of out-of-fold predictions from PLS, RSM, RF, XGBoost, GP, MLP and Hybrid, with an inner 5-fold group CV).

    LSTM on daily profiles

    Input: daily set-point profiles (temperature, cumulative feed, pH before/after shift, glucose, shaker/tip speed, air, X0). Output: VCD, IVCC and cumulative titre (monotone). VCDmax = peak of the predicted VCD trajectory. Trained jointly on both cohorts, 3 seeds × 700 epochs.

    Why do linear models blow up at the edge?

    05

    Choosing the final model

    A purely data-driven model gives flat or arbitrary answers along variables that were nearly constant in the history (initial temperature, shift temperature, seeding density, feed, shaker speed), so it cannot be trusted to optimise them. The final model = the best hybrid (kinetic backbone + residual learner) by Composite; the overall winner is reported next to it.

    06

    Parameter tuning: the kinetic backbone

    A mechanistic growth / death / nutrient / product model was fitted jointly to the VCD, viability and titre time series of both cohorts (MAP with CHO literature priors on the temperature sensitivities). Uncertainty comes from 20 refits on 80% of the batches (bootstrap).

    Equations (Euler, Δt = 0.1 d)

    dX/dt = (μ − kd)·X μ = μmax·fμ(T)·S/(Ks+S)·(1 − X/Xcap) kd = fd(T)·(kd0 + kd_tox·(IVC/100)²) + kd_s·(1 − S/(Ks+S)) dP/dt = qp·fq(T)·X·(1 − w_s·(1 − S/(Ks+S))) dS/dt = −m·X + yF·F(t)/10 fμ = exp(a_mu·ΔT − bhot·max(ΔT,0)²) fq = exp(−a_q·ΔT) fd = exp(a_d·ΔT + bhot·max(ΔT,0)²) ΔT = T − 37 °C
    ΔT uses the initial temperature before the shift and the shift temperature after it, so initial temperature, shift temperature and shift time all act on IVCC, VCDmax and QP through these equations.

        12

        Try settings by hand: simulator, glucose and agitation planners

        The final hybrid model, the fitted glucose-uptake law and a per-bioreactor agitation model run inside this page, so any combination of settings can be tested before it is put into a flask or a bioreactor. Good settings can be saved and compared.

        Dashboard

        Manual settings, glucose and agitation planning

        One settings box for RD and one for each Production line, with live titre, IVCC, VCDmax and QP ± SD. The glucose planner forecasts when glucose reaches 1 g/L or runs out and how much 400 g/L stock or Feed Alpha Plus (80 g/L) to add. The agitation planner converts tip speed to rpm for each Line 3 / Line 4 bioreactor and shows how the recipe moves VCD, viability and titre day by day.

        How agitation moves each response, by culture day

        Same setting in the other bioreactors

        Your plateau translated to every Line 3 / Line 4 bioreactor. Equal tip speed keeps shear at the impeller; equal power per volume (P/V ∝ rpm³ · D⁵ ÷ V, same impeller type) keeps mixing and gas dispersion. Use loads that speed into the planner.
